concept_options.title: The Sky Should Be Violet
concept_options.hook: By the physics, the sky should be violet. So why does it look blue?
concept_options.visual_approach: Spectrum bar that 'predicts' violet, then a reveal of sunlight's spectrum and the eye's sensitivity curve.
key_points: Less violet in sunlight + eyes favor blue
concept_options.core_message: The blue sky is physics plus biology.
concept_options.cta: Look up at the next clear sky and notice the paler blue near the horizon.
concept_options.why_this_works: Answers the follow-up question most explainers skip (UCR Physics FAQ).

concept_options.title: Sunlight, Sorted by Color
concept_options.hook: Sunlight is white. Space is black. So why is the sky blue?
concept_options.visual_approach: Follow one beam of white sunlight from the Sun into the air: it splits into colored waves, blue ones ping-pong off molecules across the sky, red ones pass straight through; ends on a sunset.
key_points: Air molecules scatter short blue waves ~5x more than red
Blue reaches you from every direction
Why not violet: less in sunlight, eyes favor blue
Sunset: long path scatters the blue away
concept_options.core_message: The blue sky is sunlight sorted by color.
concept_options.cta: Next sunset, remember: same air, same physics.
concept_options.why_this_works: A single followable journey shows the mechanism, folds in the violet twist as a mid-point surprise, and pays off with sunsets everyone has seen.

concept_options.title: Three Skies
concept_options.hook: On the Moon, the daytime sky is black. On Mars it's butterscotch. Why is ours blue?
concept_options.visual_approach: Three side-by-side worlds; air is added or removed and the sky color changes in each.
concept_options.core_message: The sky's color is the air's fingerprint.
concept_options.cta: Ask: what color would an alien sky be?
concept_options.why_this_works: Comparison makes air's role obvious (Astronomy magazine).

selected_concept.rationale: Journey structure is the clearest for a 45s general-audience piece and absorbs c1's violet twist as its mid-point surprise.
modifications: Fold in c1's 'why not violet?' beat

production_plan.art_direction: 'Light, sorted': navy space -> cerulean day -> amber sunset. Sun as a soft gold disc; light drawn as glowing sine waves in true spectral colors; air molecules as small pale-blue dots; blue waves ricochet between molecules; on-screen labels minimal, rounded sans-serif.

taste_profile.design_read: Curious-science short for a general audience: make invisible light physics feel tactile and luminous; calm wonder, not hype.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Night-space navy base that warms to daytime cerulean and ends in sunset amber; spectral wave colors (red/orange/yellow/green/blue/violet) are the only saturated accents.
taste_profile.layout_variation: Alternate wide 'sky world' frames (sun, atmosphere, horizon) with close-up 'molecule scale' frames where single waves hit single molecules.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: No generated images (no image keys): every visual is hand-drawn vector/SVG animation authored for this piece; one review still per scene at the storyboard gate.
quality_gates: Every scene shows the mechanism (waves, molecules, path length) rather than just stating it
No more than one short on-screen label per beat
